text:
For most of the first month and a half, Timo Meier did everything but score. He has 86 shots and 9.15 expected goals (the quality of his chances) in 23 games, and only six goals to show for it. Now it's turning: goals in three straight games, a four-game point streak, and Sheldon Keefe praising his ‘Excellent Game’ against Montreal, per Yahoo Sports.

Our numbers still list him as due. He's shooting 7% against a typical range near 10%, and the Devils have scored 5.8 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. Over his last ten games he made 5.0 expected goals on his own shots, more than his usual 3.9, so the streak is built on more chances, not fewer.

This is who he's been. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 87th percentile for chances from in front of the net last season, and Evolving-Hockey's adjusted numbers had New Jersey creating more with him on the ice (88th percentile). At 30, with 241 career goals before this season, the slow start looked like bad luck. The streak looks like the correction arriving.
headline: Timo Meier's goals are finally catching his chances
